To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the media in which a text is displayed influences the self regulation of learning of students with ADHD, and that this is particularly true when the conditions of comprehension favor good self regulation.
the media (digital or printed) had a different impact on reading comprehension and SRL in higher education students.
the media (digital versus print) had a significant impact on reading comprehension and on self-monitoring in higher education students.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of digital media on the learning process in higher education students.
the impact of media (digital vs print) on text comprehension and the ability to self monitor one’s performance in higher education students.
the impact of the media (i.e., digital, print) on text comprehension and SRL in higher education students (with and without ADHD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the media (print or digital) does not influence the reading comprehension and self-monitoring of higher education students with attention-deficit hyperactive disorder.
students with ADHD have more difficulties with self regulation in digital media than their peers.
students with ADHD should pay attention to the medium of the text they are reading, and be especially cautious when they read digitally displayed text.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
students with ADHD should be encouraged to use the print version of text whenever possible.
the digital condition requires more self monitoring, which is more difficult for students with ADHD.
digital text is a double edged sword for students with ADHD, as it can be both a facilitator and a barrier to comprehension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the media used to present text should be taken into account when designing learning materials for students with ADHD.
educators should pay more attention to digital text and its impact on students with ADHD.
students with ADHD need to pay attention to the media they use for reading, especially when they are required to engage in SRL activities.
